evidence: Internal unverified assumption, not a demonstrated implementation bug. The root Goal promises a 'bounded-time warning'; Message deadline contract expressly retains 'bounded deadline detection' while excluding only bounded native submission. The same contract backdates every formerly dormant obligation and says expired rows become due on the 'normal bounded scan'; Risks acknowledges an upgrade warning burst and mitigates it only with 'bound scan work'. Receipts task ht-0lo.1.2 owns bounded indexed due discovery and tests warnings pending during blocked native wake; ht-0lo.1.3 tests a bounded warning burst. Across the complete settled artifact there is no scanner cadence, maximum detection lag, backlog-dependent bound, explicit fair continuation invariant, or multi-batch completion acceptance test. Concrete dependency: an upgrade yields more expired obligations than one bounded scan can process; an obligation beyond the first batch cannot receive its durable warning until later scan progress. If blocked wake work or repeated selection of previously processed overdue work prevents that progress, its deadline stays expired indefinitely despite the running daemon. That contradicts the stated bounded detection requirement even though native submission is correctly deferred. The design requires the desired result but supplies no scheduler/progress contract or acceptance evidence excluding this failure. A finite multi-batch backlog test with blocked native wakes and an explicit maximum scan-count lag would resolve the material uncertainty without demanding unlimited-load guarantees. Should-fix rather than Blocking because the artifact does not demonstrate that the existing scanner actually lacks fairness or is coupled to native admission.
